items.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.

items.title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
items.summary: Two men tell of the work they say they have been doing to support Ukrainian intelligence during the war.

items.title: Watch: Russian saboteur working for Ukraine shares reconnaissance videos
items.summary: In a BBC World Service documentary, the man claims to have played a role in drone attacks on his home soil.

items.title: 'Postcode lottery' driving children's inequality in England, commissioner warns
items.summary: Dame Rachel De Souza's landmark report says children are being failed by a "postcode lottery".

items.title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day
items.summary: More property asking prices are being cut than at any time in 15 years, data shared with the BBC shows.

items.title: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
items.summary: Prime Minister Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".

items.title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine
items.summary: Antisocial behaviour on buses in England could lead to fines while a new campaign is also being launched for trains. A national campaign asking rail passengers "share the carriage, not the noise" is being launched.

items.title: Burnham says youth employment and training crisis is a 'moral failure'
items.summary: The UK faces "economic catastrophe" with one million young people not in work or training, the prime minister says.
